title: The Paper Regiment
premise: In 1899 London, Quentin Winterbourne serves as driver and discreet reader of correspondence for Lady Adelia Vane, a prominent suffragist whose letters Quentin quietly archives, sensing history will need them. When a gaunt stranger named Elias Crane arrives bearing letters in the unmistakable hand of Captain Rowan Vane—Adelia's brother, officially dead at Omdurman fourteen years ago—Quentin realizes the family's celebrated martyr may have deserted, survived, and been blackmailing his way through Europe. As Adelia's parliamentary allies close ranks to bury the scandal and a rival historian prepares a sanitized biography, Quentin must decide whether loyalty means protecting the legend or preserving the truth. She smuggles the real correspondence out in installments hidden among suffrage pamphlets, publishes it as an anonymous serial on the eve of 1900, and ends the century with her name finally on the record—at the cost of her invisibility and her place in the Vane household.
about_author: Wendell Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing private papers of Edwardian political families before turning to fiction. They write from a converted coach house in Kent, where they keep a wall of unsent letters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Letters
chapters.summary: Quentin Winterbourne, Lady Adelia Vane's driver, reads each letter before delivering it and files copies in a locked case under the carriage seat. POV: Quentin. Establishes her methodical invisibility and quiet conviction that paper outlives people; emotional beat: competent solitude masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Orders for the Road
chapters.summary: Adelia receives orders to travel to a memorial dedication for her brother, Captain Rowan Vane, killed at Omdurman. Quentin drives her through fog to the family estate, observing how the household performs grief. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: unease beneath ceremony, the sense that legends are being maintained rather than mourned.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Elias Crane, a shabby ex-army clerk, appears at the estate gate carrying letters written in Rowan Vane's hand—dated years after his death. He asks for Adelia and is turned away by the butler. POV: Quentin, watching from the drive. Emotional beat: electric recognition that the official story has a crack in it.

chapters.title: The Hand That Would Not Die
chapters.summary: Quentin intercepts one of Crane's letters and compares it against archived correspondence: the handwriting is Rowan's beyond doubt. She confronts Crane privately; he claims Rowan lives, disgraced, and wants restitution. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: vertigo—the archivist realizing the archive lies.

chapters.title: What the Lady Knows
chapters.summary: Quentin weighs telling Adelia, then discovers a suppressed letter suggesting Adelia already suspects her brother survived. Family honor versus truth begins its war inside the house. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: betrayal of trust in both directions—she has read what was never meant for her.

chapters.title: The Historian's Visit
chapters.summary: Sir Godfrey Mace, biographer preparing the authorized life of Rowan Vane, arrives to collect papers and sanitize the record. Quentin watches him cherry-pick documents and burn others. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: cold anger; she understands the victors are writing history in real time.

chapters.title: Crane's Price
chapters.summary: Crane reveals he was Rowan's accomplice in desertion and blackmail, now seeking payment or exposure—he no longer cares which. Quentin negotiates time, hiding him in a coaching inn. POV: alternating Quentin and Crane. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance between two people who live off other people's secrets.

chapters.title: The Deserted Man
chapters.summary: Through Crane's testimony, Rowan's true story emerges: he fled Omdurman before the battle, lived under false names, and extorted his own family to stay hidden. POV: Crane recounting, framed by Quentin. Emotional beat: pity curdling into judgment; heroism revealed as performance.

chapters.title: Adelia's Silence
chapters.summary: Quentin finally shows Adelia the evidence. Adelia admits she has suspected for years and chose the legend because the cause—the suffrage movement—needs its martyrs clean. POV: Adelia, first time. Emotional beat: heartbreak of a woman choosing usefulness over truth.

chapters.title: Measured in What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mace learns of Crane and moves to have him arrested for blackmail, which would silence the whole affair. Quentin must move the archive—every copied letter—out of the house in a single night. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: her lifelong question made literal; the carriage becomes a library in flight.

chapters.title: The Case Under the Seat
chapters.summary: Quentin smuggles the correspondence to a printing friend, Miss Okafor, who runs a small radical press. They plan an anonymous serial: 'Letters of a Living Dead Man.' POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration—reading letters becomes publishing them.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Adelia offers Quentin money and a reference to leave quietly, believing dismissal will protect her. Quentin refuses, revealing she knows about the suppression. POV: both women. Emotional beat: the servant's invisible labor made visible; the relationship breaks open.

chapters.title: Crane Taken
chapters.summary: Mace's agents find Crane; he is arrested and the press threatens to trace the letters back to the Vane household. Quentin realizes her copies are now the only uncorrupted record. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: guilt—her ally fell because of her timeline.

chapters.title: The First Installment
chapters.summary: The serial's first installment appears in three radical weeklies; London wakes to the rumor that Captain Vane lives. Mace scrambles, Adelia's allies demand denials. POV: shifting public voice anchored in Quentin. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, frightening power of print.

chapters.title: Hunted Reader
chapters.summary: Detectives trace distribution routes toward Miss Okafor's press. Quentin leads them astray using her driver's knowledge of the city, sacrificing her own safety. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the invisible woman weaponizing her invisibility.

chapters.title: Rowan Comes Home
chapters.summary: Rowan Vane himself surfaces, drawn back by the publicity, half wanting confession, half wanting payment for silence. He meets Quentin in a railway hotel. POV: Rowan. Emotional beat: pathetic grandeur—a man meeting the consequences he outran for fourteen years.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Midnight
chapters.summary: Rowan offers Quentin the original letters if she kills the serial; Mace offers her legitimacy if she hands over her archive. Between them stands the truth. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: temptation from both directions; her integrity priced and refused.

chapters.title: What Adelia Does
chapters.summary: Cornered, Adelia makes her choice: she publicly confirms the letters' authenticity, sacrificing her brother's legend to save the movement's credibility—and, secretly, to free herself. POV: Adelia. Emotional beat: catharsis; the lie had been heavier than the truth.

chapters.title: Trial by Column Inch
chapters.summary: The final installments run; courts, journalists, and Parliament converge. Crane, released on the strength of the published evidence, testifies. Mace's biography collapses. POV: ensemble, centered on Quentin watching from the gallery. Emotional beat: vindication arriving loudly after years of quiet work.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: New Year's Eve, 1899. Quentin walks through celebratory crowds carrying nothing but her name, deciding whether to sign the final installment. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: threshold dread and hope; the old century's secrets dying with it.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Quentin signs the last installment with her full name and appends her archive's provenance, ensuring historians cannot erase how the truth surfaced. Adelia, publicly humbled, hires her back—not as a driver, but as keeper of the papers. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: identity claimed at last; inheritance redefined as stewardship of truth.

chapters.title: The Paper Regiment Marches
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring 1900: Quentin opens the Vane archive to researchers, including young suffragists who will carry the story forward. A new letter arrives; she reads it first, as always—but now writes her own account beside it. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; justice outside the law, preserved on paper.
